chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khath'ami, from 'Abd al-Rahim al-Qasir, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about something from Divine Unity, so he raised his hands to the sky and said: 'Exalted is Allah, the Supreme [Jabbar]. Verily, whoever speculates about what is there will be destroyed.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Imam mean by 'whoever speculates about Divine Unity will be destroyed'?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) demonstrates the Shia doctrine of *ta'awwul* (speculative theology) by raising his hands to signify God's absolute transcendence (*tanzih*) beyond human comprehension. The warning that 'he who engages with it perishes' underscores the scholarly consensus that while basic Tawhid is obligatory, deep metaphysical debate regarding Allah's essence can lead to error or spiritual ruin if not approached with caution.
